references.text: Mount Gerizim is mentioned here as the place where the blessings were to be read, the same mountain where Jotham stood and spoke to the men of Shechem.
Mount Gerizim is the designated place for blessing, and Jotham used this symbolic location to address the people in Shechem.
Joshua reads the blessings and curses at Gerizim and Ebal, the same place Jotham later uses for his speech.
The context of Jotham's speech: Abimelech had just been made king in Shechem after killing his brothers.
Shechem is an important place in the history of the patriarchs, where Abraham first received the promise of the land.
The call to 'listen to me' and the desire that God should hear reflect the Psalmist's prayer for God to listen.
Isaiah also calls on heaven and earth to listen, a similar rhetorical appeal as in Jotham's speech.
